name: HUD Fair Market Rents (FMR) — county/metro and Small Area (ZIP-level) 40th-percentile gross rent estimates
gap: gross_rent_yield (valuation pillar) and the per-property rent assumption in investment.py both currently depend on Zillow ZORI, which this project's own adapter (zillow_research.py) hard-filters to NYC ZIP codes in NYC counties. There is no rent series at all that covers counties outside NYC, so the valuation pillar and the whole investment-math module would silently have no rent data the moment the project is pointed at a non-NYC area.
coverage: national — every US county/metro, every fiscal year since FY1983; Small Area FMRs give ZIP-level detail within large metros
granularity: county/metro (standard FMR) or ZIP (Small Area FMR, used mainly in larger metros including NYC)
update_frequency: annual (new fiscal-year file published by October 1 each year, by law)
license: US government work (HUD), public domain, no login or key required for the static downloads.
cost: Free; no rate limit on the static CSV/Excel downloads. A programmatic API also exists (huduser.gov) but documentation for it is thinner than the plain file downloads.
recommendation: Recommend as a fallback/complement, not a replacement for ZORI. FMR is a regulatory estimate (40th-percentile 'standard quality' rent for Section 8 purposes) rather than a market-rate index, so it's a noisier proxy for condo asking rents than ZORI where ZORI is available — but it is the only free rent series with literally national county coverage, which ZORI (even unfiltered) doesn't guarantee for small/rural counties. Good value as a documented fallback for gross_rent_yield and investment.py's rent assumption whenever a target area has no ZORI coverage, directly supporting the project's 'any US neighborhood' goal. Lower priority than the mortgage-rate and FHFA candidates since it only matters once non-NYC areas are actually being screened.
